summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with Enterobacter bacteremia, likely originating from his tunneled central venous catheter, which was confirmed by positive tip culture. He also had multifocal pneumonia and worsening ascites requiring multiple therapeutic paracenteses. He developed acute kidney injury, consistent with hepatorenal syndrome type 2, which stabilized with albumin and discontinuation of diuretics. His portopulmonary hypertension worsened, with echocardiogram showing increased pulmonary artery pressure. He completed a 14-day course of IV antibiotics, with clearance of bacteremia. His condition improved, and he was discharged home on oral ciprofloxacin for SBP prophylaxis, with plans for outpatient follow-up, repeat blood cultures, and eventual tunneled line replacement.
problems: Bloodstream infection due to central venous catheter
